subject.title: Feature Request: Masked Secrets - Prevent Agent from Accessing Raw API Keys

question: What credential-confidentiality guarantee should OpenClaw provide when an agent invokes a tool or command that needs a secret?
rationale: The choice determines whether core owns a capability broker, only strengthens managed SecretRefs, or formally delegates arbitrary-command isolation to plugins and the operating system; substitution and redaction mechanics cannot decide that threat model safely.

options.title: Capability broker boundary
options.body: Add an owned broker or provider contract that gives tools capabilities rather than raw values and injects credentials only at final dispatch, with persistence-safe output redaction and upgrade tests.

options.title: Managed credentials only
options.body: Guarantee protection only for OpenClaw-managed provider, channel, and plugin credentials, while documenting OS isolation or external proxies for arbitrary shell commands.

options.title: Plugin-led boundary
options.body: Standardize and document the existing hook-based credential-provider pattern while keeping raw arbitrary-command credential isolation outside core.

recommendation.title: Capability broker boundary
recommendation.body: Add an owned broker or provider contract that gives tools capabilities rather than raw values and injects credentials only at final dispatch, with persistence-safe output redaction and upgrade tests.

likelyOwner.reason: Their merged work owns the current SecretRef, sentinel, redaction, and migration architecture that this decision would extend or delimit.
